B-INDEPENDENT-REGIME-NULL.description: Regime-independent bank matched in marginals; regime fixed per trajectory, R from (cur_state, action) only

B-IID-MARGINAL-NULL.description: IID resampled S_next from positive bank marginal

B-HISTORY-MARKOV.description: Order-3 history-only baseline (not computed separately in this run)

CTRL_POS_NONCOPY_REGIME.description: Non-copy regime-injected positive bank; regime switches within trajectory, R from stochastic mixing channel

CTRL_ANALYTIC_CENTERING.description: G0 analytic centering: |perm_mean - analytic_mean| < 0.03 and |analytic_mean| < 0.1 per R per bank

observations: Null bank (B-INDEPENDENT-REGIME-NULL) returns p_bonf=1.0 and BC≈0 on all four R channels, satisfying G1 (null validity gate).
Positive bank (CTRL_POS_NONCOPY_REGIME) returns p_bonf=1.0 and BC=0 on all four R channels, failing G2 (sensitivity gate requires p_bonf<0.01, BC>0.05, gap≥0.05).

Analytic null expectation (G0) yields analytic_mean≈5.09 bits (null) and ≈3.81 bits (positive), far exceeding the |analytic_mean|<0.1 requirement; consistency |perm_mean-analytic_mean|≈4.3 and ≈3.0, far exceeding 0.03. G0 fails on all channels for both banks.

Identifiability (G3) fails: MI(R;regime)≈0.99 (>0.3 passes) but MI(R;latent_state_index)≈2.26 (>0.9 fails) on all channels. The 4-char hash space (65536 values) with 25 (cur_state,action) combinations still yields near-deterministic mapping from latent state to R.

Permutation distribution shows zero variance (perm_std=0) because the DM plug-in estimator with shared K,alpha yields H(S_next|C)=H(S_next|C,R) for all permutations - the estimator cannot detect the regime signal in R.
Both banks have ~440 strata with ~2-3 samples each in TRAIN, causing extreme finite-sample bias in the analytic formula (E[PMI] ≈ 3-5 bits instead of ≈0).
validity_notes: G0 analytic formula (E[PMI] via digamma) produces large positive bias (~3-5 bits) under the frozen design (40 trajectories × 40 steps, 5 states, H_K=3 history → ~440 strata, ~2.5 samples/stratum). This bias is a known property of the plug-in estimator with small N_c; the permutation test correctly captures it (perm_mean≈0, but analytic_mean≈5). The gate threshold |analytic_mean|<0.1 is unattainable with this design.

G2 sensitivity fails because the DM plug-in estimator with shared K,alpha yields identical entropy H(S_next|C) = H(S_next|C,R) for all R channels. The regime signal in R does not reduce conditional entropy because: (a) C=(URL_before, history) nearly identifies the trajectory, and regime switches every 10 steps within trajectory, so C contains partial regime information; (b) the estimator's sub-strata (C,R) have too few samples (often 1) for reliable entropy estimation.

G3 identifiability fails because MI(R;latent_state_index)≈2.26 > 0.9. The 4-char hash (16 bits) with only 25 input combinations still acts as a near-injective function of (cur_state, action). To achieve MI<0.9 would require either a much smaller hash space (≤3 bits) or removing latent_state from R generation - but the frozen spec requires R to be generated from (cur_state, action, regime).

The frozen design (spec.json, prereg.md) specifies 40×40 transitions with H_K=3 history, which creates too many strata for the analytic null to be accurate. This is a design-level validity threat, not an execution error.
No browser, CDP, Playwright, or network calls were used - purely in-process synthetic banks as mandated.
TRAIN/TEST split (70/30 by trajectory_id) and all fitting (strata, vocabularies, K, alpha) performed on TRAIN only as specified.
Permutation test: 1000 trajectory-grouped shuffles within each C stratum, seed 42, PYTHONHASHSEED=0.
unresolved: Whether any variant of the pointwise conditional PMI paradigm can pass G0 with the frozen design parameters (40×40, 5 states, H_K=3). The analytic bias is fundamental to the estimator/strata combination.

Whether the regime signal can be made detectable (G2) while keeping MI(R;latent)<0.9 (G3) under the frozen R generation constraints. The two requirements are in tension: regime must affect R detectably but not make R a deterministic function of latent state.
Whether increasing hash collision (shorter hash) or noise rate could simultaneously satisfy G2 and G3 without violating the frozen spec's R channel descriptions.
Whether a different entropy estimator (NSB, Miller-Madow) would yield non-zero BC on the positive bank with this data.
